United Oil & Gas plc
("United" or "the Company")
Award of Share Options
United Oil & Gas Plc (AIM: "UOG"), the oil and gas company with a high-impact exploration asset in Jamaica and a development asset in the UK, announces that, the Company on the 18 August 2026 awarded in total 203,814,481 share options under its updated unapproved share option scheme details of which were disclosed in the Remuneration Committee Report in the Company's 2025 Accounts. 97,932,799 share options (representing 2.11% of the Company's current issued share capital) have been awarded to employees and consultants whilst the further 105,881,682 share options (representing 2.28% of the Company's current issued share capital) have been awarded to PDMRs as detailed below:

Key Terms of the Awards:
a) Exercise price of £0.0024 per ordinary share, which is a 20% premium to the price of Company's July 2026 fundraising.
b) Vesting period of one year from date of grant.
c) Performance criterion: share options vest only if the Company's share price reaches £0.006 per ordinary share, representing a 250% increase on the share option price and 300% on the July 2026 placing price.
d) The share options will be valid for 10 years from date of issue.
Following this award, the total number of share options in issue is 575,403,278 representing approximately 12.41% of the Company's current issued share capital of 4,636,021,868 ordinary shares.
These awards are designed to align management incentives directly with shareholder value creation, ensuring that any benefit to participants is realised only following a material increase in the Company's share price.
Related Party Transaction:
The award of new share options to Brian Larkin, the Company's Director and CEO, Iman Hill, the Company's Non-Executive Director, and Simon Brett, the Company's Chief Financial Officer (Non-Board), pursuant to the updated unapproved share option scheme, is regarded as a related party transaction under the AIM Rules. Accordingly, David Williams, being the independent director for the purposes of considering the share option award, considers that the terms of the award are fair and reasonable insofar as the Company's shareholders are concerned.

THIS ANNOUNCEMENT CONTAINS INSIDE INFORMATION FOR THE PURPOSES OF REGULATION (EU) 596/2014 AS IT FORMS PART OF DOMESTIC LAW IN THE UNITED KINGDOM BY VIRTUE OF THE EU (WITHDRAWAL) ACT 2018 ("MAR"). IN ADDITION, MARKET SOUNDINGS (AS DEFINED IN MAR) WERE TAKEN IN RESPECT OF THE PLACING WITH THE RESULT THAT CERTAIN PERSONS BECAME AWARE OF INSIDE INFORMATION (AS DEFINED IN MAR), AS PERMITTED BY MAR. THIS INSIDE INFORMATION IS SET OUT IN THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. THEREFORE, THOSE PERSONS THAT RECEIVED INSIDE INFORMATION IN A MARKET SOUNDING ARE NO LONGER IN POSSESSION OF SUCH INSIDE INFORMATION RELATING TO THE COMPANY AND ITS SECURITIES.
United Oil & Gas PLC / Index: AIM / Epic: UOG / Sector: Oil & Gas
3rd July 2026
United Oil and Gas plc
("United" or "the Company")
£500,000 Capital Raise
United Oil & Gas Plc (AIM: "UOG"), the oil and gas company with a high impact exploration asset in Jamaica and a development asset in the UK is pleased to announce a placing of 250,000,000 new ordinary shares of 0.001p each (the "Placing Shares") at a price of 0.20p per share ("Issue Price"), raising gross proceeds of £500,000 before expenses, by two long term institutional shareholders (the "Placing")
arranged by Tennyson Securities. The Issue Price represents a modest discount to the closing mid-market price of 0.23p on 2 July 2026 being the last day prior to the publication of this announcement.
Net proceeds will be applied to strengthen the Company's working capital position as it continues to advance the farm-out of the Walton-Morant Licence. Each placee will receive one warrant for every three Placing Shares subscribed, exercisable at 0.28p per share for 6 months from the date of issue.
Brian Larkin, CEO, commented:
"This Placing, by existing two long term institutional shareholders who know this Company and its assets well, strengthens our working capital at a point when the technical work is complete and the farm-out process is active and progressing. Securing additional working capital under current more favourable market conditions is in our view the prudent course, both for the Company and for shareholders.
We remain focused on progressing the farm-out and will update the market as and when appropriate."
Settlement and Admission
Application will be made to the London Stock Exchange for admission of the 250,000,000 Placing Shares to trading on AIM (the "Admission"). It is expected that Admission will become effective and that dealings in the Placing Shares will commence at 8.00 a.m. on or around 9 July 2026.
Total Voting Rights
Following admission of the Placing Shares, the Company's enlarged issued share capital will comprise 4,636,021,868 ordinary shares. This figure may be used by shareholders as the denominator for calculations to determine whether they are required to notify their interest in the Company under the FCA's Disclosure Guidance and Transparency Rules.
**ENDS**

company_30s.what_they_do: UOG is an offshore oil exploration company that focuses on seismic surveys and drilling in under‑explored basins, mainly around Jamaica and the Caribbean.
company_30s.why_they_matter: Oil and gas remain the backbone of global energy supply, and UOG’s projects sit in regions that could hold untapped reserves. Their work could add to the supply chain and provide new opportunities for larger majors looking to partner or acquire proven assets.
company_30s.current_state: The firm has just raised £500,000 and finished a key seismic survey, signalling it is moving toward the drilling phase. It is still a small, thin‑liquidity play that trades at a steep discount to any previous highs, reflecting its high‑risk, high‑reward nature.

rns_narrative: UOG has been busy with a mix of funding and exploration milestones: a fresh capital raise, updates on regulatory status, and the completion of a seismic survey in Jamaica.
Corporate governance is also in motion – AGM notices, board appointments, and share‑option awards show the company is keeping its structure in order.
The overall story is one of a company that is still very much in the pre‑drill, pre‑reserve phase but is actively clearing obstacles that could enable a first‑well push.

crowd_tape.dominant_theme: Quiet but hopeful – the community is largely silent, with a few whispers of optimism around potential drilling results.
crowd_tape.bull_narrative: A handful of traders point to insider buying and the recent capital raise as signs that smart money believes in a turnaround.
crowd_tape.bear_narrative: Others worry that the company could face regulatory delays, dilution from further fundraising, or that the seismic data may not translate into commercial reserves.
crowd_tape.sentiment_shift: The mood has stayed flat; no new buzz has emerged, which for a contrarian means a perfect set‑up for surprise if a positive catalyst hits.

whats_happening_now.attention_check: Google Trends for UOG is flat – no public search interest, which signals that the market has not yet priced in any upcoming news.

near_term_catalysts: A positive drilling result from the Jamaica program – the company is due to announce core data in the next quarter.
Regulatory approval for a drilling permit, which would clear the last hurdle before a well can be started.
A sudden spike in trading volume that shows institutional interest, especially if the price moves above the 20‑day moving average.
Any announcement of a partnership or joint venture with a larger oil operator that could bring in expertise and capital.
expect_next.watch_for: Confirm the above by looking for: 1) a press release with seismic interpretation or drilling results; 2) a regulatory filing that clears the next stage; 3) a breakout above the 20‑day SMA with volume at least twice the average; 4) a share price move to the 50‑day high. If any of these fail to materialise, the risk of a further decline rises.
expect_next.timing_regime: The stock appears to be in the early phase of a deep crash – the market has likely finished capitulating. With the APEX compression score high, the next move will be a mean‑reversion once one of the catalysts above plays out.

buy_vs_sell.bull_case: UOG is a classic deep‑crashed play. Historically, a 70‑95% drop can deliver 160%+ returns once the bounce begins. The recent capital raise and survey completion reduce downside risk, while a positive drilling result would lift the price to roughly half of its all‑time high – a 100‑200% upside with a very small risk of a further 10‑20% decline.
buy_vs_sell.bear_case: The company still faces regulatory uncertainty and low liquidity. If the seismic data turns out to be dry or the company cannot secure a drilling permit, the price could slide another 10‑15% before settling at a new low. Dilution from future fund‑raises is also a risk.
buy_vs_sell.risk_reward: Potential upside 1.5–2× the current price versus a downside of only 10‑15% if the market corrects. The asymmetry is favourable for a contrarian long.

playbook.if_bullish: Enter after the stock closes above the 20‑day SMA with volume >2× the 20‑day average. Allocate 5–7% of your portfolio to the position and set a stop 10% below the recent low. Target a 50% gain if the price recovers to halfway between the current level and the all‑time high.
